approach: All cyclic shifts of s correspond to length-n windows in the doubled string s + s. Use a sliding window of size n to track mismatches against alternating patterns "0101..." and "1010...", finding the minimum flips in O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Check if Binary String Has at Most One Segment of Ones
summary: Check if a binary string without leading zeros contains at most one contiguous segment of ones.
approach: Since s has no leading zeros (s[0] == 1), all ones in the first segment start at index 0. A second segment of ones can only exist if a 1 occurs after at least one 0, which corresponds to the substring "01". Return true if "01" is not present, otherwise false in O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Minimum Changes To Make Alternating Binary String
summary: Return the minimum number of operations needed to make a binary string alternating.
approach: There are only two valid alternating binary strings of length n: starting with '0' (0101...) or starting with '1' (1010...). Count the mismatches with the pattern starting with '0' as diff0. Since the two patterns are complementary, the mismatches with the second pattern is n - diff0. The answer is min(diff0, n - diff0) in O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Special Positions in a Binary Matrix
summary: Return the count of special positions in a binary matrix where a position (i, j) is special if mat[i][j] == 1 and all other elements in row i and column j are 0.
approach: Precompute row sums and column sums in O(m * n) time. A position (i, j) is special if mat[i][j] == 1, rowSum[i] == 1, and colSum[j] == 1.

title: Find Kth Bit in Nth Binary String
summary: Return the k-th bit in the n-th generated binary string formed recursively via concatenation, reversal, and inversion.
approach: Exploit the recursive symmetry of the sequence: center bit is '1', left half is identical to S_{n-1}, and right half is reversed and inverted, solving iteratively in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

title: Minimum Swaps to Arrange a Binary Grid
summary: Find the minimum number of adjacent row swaps needed to make all cells above the main diagonal zeros, or return -1 if impossible.
approach: Count trailing zeros for each row. For each row position i, greedily find the first available row with at least (n - 1 - i) trailing zeros, add the swap distance, and bubble it up to position i.

title: Partitioning Into Minimum Number Of Deci-Binary Numbers
summary: Find the minimum number of positive deci-binary numbers needed to sum up to a given decimal number string n.
approach: Since each deci-binary number contributes at most 1 at each column with 0 carries, the minimum number of deci-binary numbers needed is simply the maximum digit in n. Iterate through n and return the maximum digit, exiting immediately if 9 is found.

title: Concatenation of Consecutive Binary Numbers
summary: Concatenate the binary representations of numbers from 1 to n into a single binary number and compute its decimal value modulo 10^9 + 7.
approach: Iterate from 1 to n while tracking current bit length which increments whenever i is a power of 2 using (i & (i - 1)) == 0. In each step, shift the accumulated answer left by bit length, bitwise OR with i, and take modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Minimum Operations to Equalize Binary String
summary: Find the minimum number of k-bit flips required to transform all characters in a binary string into 1s.
approach: Analyze flip parity and total capacity bounds via Gale-Ryser realizability, calculating minimal odd and even operation counts in O(1) arithmetic after an initial O(n) count of zeros.

title: Number of Steps to Reduce a Number in Binary Representation to One
summary: Count the number of steps to reduce a binary number to 1 by dividing by 2 if even or adding 1 if odd.
approach: Simulate arithmetic right-to-left tracking carry: an odd bit requires 2 steps (add 1 + divide by 2) setting carry to 1, while an even bit requires 1 step (divide by 2) in O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Sort Integers by The Number of 1 Bits
summary: Sort an integer array by the number of 1-bits ascending, breaking ties by numerical value.
approach: Encode each number as bitCount * 10001 + originalValue to sort directly on the primitive array in-place, then decode with modulo 10001 in O(N log N) time and O(1) space.

title: Sum of Root To Leaf Binary Numbers
summary: Calculate the total sum of binary numbers formed along all root-to-leaf paths in a binary tree.
approach: Traverse the binary tree using depth-first search (DFS), incrementally computing the accumulated binary value via bitwise left-shift and OR, returning the value at leaf nodes in O(N) time and O(H) auxiliary space.

title: Check If a String Contains All Binary Codes of Size K
summary: Determine whether a binary string contains all 2^k binary codes of length k as substrings.
approach: Prune using the Pigeonhole Principle if s is too short, then slide a rolling bitmask window of size k and record seen codes in a boolean array of size 2^k in O(n) time and O(2^k) space.

title: Binary Gap
summary: Find the maximum distance between any two adjacent 1s in the binary representation of an integer.
approach: Scan the binary representation of n using bitwise shifts, record the indices of set bits, and compute the maximum distance between consecutively observed 1-bits in O(log n) time and O(1) space.

title: Prime Number of Set Bits in Binary Representation
summary: Count numbers in a range having a prime number of set bits in their binary representation.
approach: Encode prime bit counts up to 19 as a bitmask (665772) and check each integer's population count against the mask in O(1) time and O(1) space.

title: Special Binary String
summary: Find the lexicographically largest resulting string by repeatedly swapping consecutive special binary substrings.
approach: Model the special binary string as a Dyck path (valid parentheses), recursively optimize each primitive block's inner substring, and greedily sort the top-level blocks in descending order.

title: Count Binary Substrings
summary: Count the number of non-empty substrings with equal numbers of consecutive 0s and 1s grouped together.
approach: Count contiguous blocks of identical characters on the fly using prevRun and currRun. Accumulate min(prevRun, currRun) for each transition in O(n) time and O(1) space.

title: Binary Number with Alternating Bits
summary: Check whether a given positive integer has strictly alternating bits in its binary representation.
approach: XOR n with n >> 1 to obtain a bitmask x. If n has alternating bits, x is a contiguous sequence of 1s satisfying (x & (x + 1)) == 0 in O(1) time.

title: Binary Watch
summary: Return all possible valid clock times represented by a binary watch when exactly turnedOn LEDs are lit.
approach: Enumerate all 720 valid clock pairs (12 hours x 60 minutes) in O(1) time. For each pair, check if bitCount(h) + bitCount(m) == turnedOn and format the time with proper zero padding.

title: Reverse Bits
summary: Reverse the binary bits of a given 32-bit unsigned/signed integer.
approach: Iterate across 32 bit positions, extracting the least significant bit with n & 1, shifting it into the result with result = (result << 1) | bit, and shifting n logically to the right with n >>>= 1 in O(1) time.

title: Add Binary
summary: Given two binary strings a and b, return their sum as a binary string.
approach: Perform base-2 column addition from right to left using two pointers and a carry variable. Append sum % 2 and propagate carry = sum / 2 until all bits and carry are exhausted, reversing the buffer at the end.

title: Champagne Tower
summary: Simulate pouring champagne into a stacked glass pyramid and return how full a specific glass at (query_row, query_glass) is.
approach: Simulate cascading liquid overflow row by row with a 2D dynamic programming array. Liquid beyond 1 cup splits equally into (r+1, c) and (r+1, c+1), clamping the requested glass value to 1.0 at the end.

title: Longest Balanced Substring II
summary: Find the length of the longest substring composed only of 'a', 'b', and 'c' where all distinct characters appear the same number of times.
approach: Decompose into cases with 1, 2, or 3 distinct characters. Use consecutive identical run tracking for 1 char, delimiter segmentation and 1D prefix difference for 2 chars, and 2D prefix difference state (cnt[a]-cnt[b], cnt[b]-cnt[c]) with a hash map for 3 chars in O(n) total time.

title: Longest Balanced Substring I
summary: Find the length of the longest substring in s where all distinct characters appear the same number of times.
approach: Enumerate candidate substring windows starting at index i with a size-26 frequency table. Validate balance in O(1) time using the invariant len == distinct * maxFreq and break early if remaining characters cannot exceed maxLen.

title: Longest Balanced Subarray II
summary: Find the length of the longest subarray in nums that contains an equal number of distinct even integers and distinct odd integers.
approach: Maintain balance scores across all left endpoints using a lazy Segment Tree. When extending to right endpoint r, perform range addition on [prev + 1, r] with parity weight, and query the smallest left endpoint with balance 0 in O(log n) using the discrete intermediate value theorem.

title: Longest Balanced Subarray I
summary: Find the length of the longest subarray in nums that contains an equal number of distinct even integers and distinct odd integers.
approach: Enumerate all candidate subarrays starting at index i using a global timestamp array lastSeen to track distinct even and distinct odd frequencies in O(1) time without reallocations, tracking the maximum length where distinctEven == distinctOdd.

title: Balance a Binary Search Tree
summary: Convert an arbitrary binary search tree into a height-balanced binary search tree with minimal depth using the same node values.
approach: Extract nodes into a sorted array using in-order traversal, then recursively construct a height-balanced BST using divide and conquer by picking the middle element at each step.

title: Balanced Binary Tree
summary: Determine whether a binary tree is height-balanced, meaning the height difference between the left and right subtrees of every node never exceeds one.
approach: Perform a bottom-up post-order DFS traversal. Return the subtree height if height-balanced or -1 sentinel upon detecting an imbalance (|left - right| > 1), avoiding redundant recalculations in O(n) linear time.

title: Minimum Deletions to Make String Balanced
summary: Find the minimum number of deletions needed to make a string consisting of a and b balanced such that no b appears before any a.
approach: Maintain running counts in a single pass: count b occurrences so far, and upon encountering a, choose greedily/dynamically between deleting this a (deletions + 1) or keeping this a by deleting all previous b characters (bCount).

title: Minimum Removals to Balance Array
summary: Find the minimum number of elements to remove from nums so that the maximum element of the remaining non-empty array is at most k times the minimum element.
approach: Sort the array and maximize the number of kept elements using two pointers / sliding window. For each minimum element at nums[left], expand the right pointer while nums[right] <= (long) nums[left] * k, returning n - maxKept.

title: Transformed Array
summary: Construct a transformed array by moving nums[i] steps right if positive, abs(nums[i]) steps left if negative, or staying at index i if zero in a circular array.
approach: Unify circular array transitions using modular arithmetic: for each index i, compute targetIndex = ((i + nums[i]) % n + n) % n and set result[i] = nums[targetIndex] in a single O(n) pass.

title: Trionic Array II
summary: Find the maximum sum of any trionic subarray in nums satisfying l < p < q < r such that nums[l...p] is strictly increasing, nums[p...q] is strictly decreasing, and nums[q...r] is strictly increasing.
approach: Identify all maximal strictly decreasing segments [p...q] with peak condition nums[p-1] < nums[p] and valley condition nums[q] < nums[q+1]. Maximize the adjacent strictly increasing runs using Kadane-style DP arrays (leftInc for suffix ending at p-1 and rightInc for prefix starting at q+1), computing the maximum total sum in O(n) linear time.

title: Trionic Array I
summary: Determine if an integer array can be partitioned into three contiguous segments: strictly increasing, strictly decreasing, and strictly increasing.
approach: Perform a single-pass three-phase linear traversal. First, climb strictly increasing elements to locate peak p (validating 0 < p < n - 2). Next, descend strictly decreasing elements to find valley q (validating p < q < n - 1). Finally, climb strictly increasing elements to the end, returning true if the pointer reaches index n - 1.

title: Divide an Array Into Subarrays With Minimum Cost II
summary: Divide an array into k contiguous subarrays minimizing the sum of their starting elements, where the starting index difference between the 2nd and kth subarray is at most dist.
approach: Since nums[0] is fixed, the problem reduces to finding a sliding window of size at most dist + 1 across nums[1 ... n - 1] that minimizes the sum of its k - 1 smallest elements. We dynamically maintain the k - 1 smallest elements using two balanced sets (or a Fenwick Tree) in O(N log(dist)) time.

title: Divide an Array Into Subarrays With Minimum Cost I
summary: Divide an array into 3 disjoint contiguous non-empty subarrays to minimize the sum of their first elements.
approach: The first subarray always starts at index 0, contributing nums[0] to the cost. The remaining two subarrays must start at two distinct indices in nums[1 ... n - 1]. To minimize the sum, identify the two smallest elements in nums[1 ... n - 1] in a single linear pass and add them to nums[0].

title: Find Smallest Letter Greater Than Target
summary: Find the smallest character in a sorted character array that is lexicographically greater than target, wrapping around to the first element if none exists.
approach: Apply upper bound binary search to locate the first character strictly greater than target in logarithmic time, using modulo arithmetic for wrap-around.

title: Minimum Cost to Convert String II
summary: Find the minimum cost to convert string source to target using substring conversion operations where chosen substrings must be either disjoint or identical.
approach: Model substring conversion rules as a directed weighted graph over unique substring tokens, compute all-pairs shortest paths using the Floyd-Warshall algorithm, and partition the string with 1D dynamic programming.

title: Minimum Cost to Convert String I
summary: Find the minimum cost to convert string source to target using character transformation rules with given individual replacement costs.
approach: Model character transformations as a directed weighted graph on 26 lowercase English letters, compute all-pairs shortest paths using the Floyd-Warshall algorithm, and sum optimal character replacement costs.

title: Minimum Cost Path with Teleportations
summary: Find the minimum total cost to reach the bottom-right cell from the top-left cell in a grid with right/down moves and up to k free teleportations to cells of less than or equal value.
approach: Layered dynamic programming over the number of teleportations t in [0, k], optimizing teleport transitions via suffix minimums across grid cell values and normal moves via 2D DAG relaxation.

title: Minimum Cost Path with Edge Reversals
summary: Find the minimum total cost to travel from node 0 to node n - 1 where each node's switch can reverse an incoming edge at double cost.
approach: Model as an augmented directed graph adding reverse edges with doubled cost, then execute Dijkstra's algorithm to compute the shortest path.

title: Minimum Absolute Difference
summary: Find all pairs of distinct integers in an array that achieve the minimum absolute difference, returned in ascending order.
approach: Sort the array in ascending order and scan adjacent elements to determine the minimum difference, then collect all adjacent pairs matching this minimum difference.

title: Minimum Difference Between Highest and Lowest of K Scores
summary: Pick any k student scores to minimize the difference between the highest and lowest scores.
approach: Sort the array and slide a fixed window of size k across all elements, computing nums[i + k - 1] - nums[i] and tracking the minimum difference.

title: Minimize Maximum Pair Sum in Array
summary: Pair up even-length array elements such that each element is in exactly one pair and the maximum pair sum is minimized.
approach: Sort the array in non-decreasing order and greedily pair the i-th smallest element with the i-th largest element (nums[i] + nums[n - 1 - i]) using two pointers, keeping track of the maximum pair sum.

title: Minimum Pair Removal to Sort Array II
summary: Repeatedly collapse the minimum sum adjacent pair until the array is non-decreasing for arrays up to 10^5 elements, returning the operation count.
approach: Maintain elements in a doubly linked list, adjacent pair sums in a Min-Heap with lazy version invalidation, and track adjacent inversions in O(1) to terminate immediately when sorted.

title: Minimum Pair Removal to Sort Array I
summary: Repeatedly replace the adjacent pair with the minimum sum with their sum until the array becomes non-decreasing, returning the number of operations performed.
approach: Simulate the process directly: while the array is not non-decreasing, locate the leftmost adjacent pair with minimum sum, replace both elements with their sum, and increment the operation count.

title: Construct the Minimum Bitwise Array II
summary: Construct an array ans such that ans[i] OR (ans[i] + 1) == nums[i] with minimized values for numbers up to 10^9, or -1 if impossible.
approach: For even prime 2, return -1 as x OR (x + 1) is always odd. For odd primes, isolate the lowest set bit of (p + 1) and clear the highest bit of the trailing 1s in p in O(1): p - (((p + 1) & -(p + 1)) >> 1).

title: Construct the Minimum Bitwise Array I
summary: Construct an array ans such that ans[i] OR (ans[i] + 1) == nums[i] with minimized values, or -1 if no such value exists.
approach: For even prime 2, return -1 as x OR (x + 1) is always odd. For odd primes, clear the highest bit in the block of trailing 1s of nums[i] using the O(1) lowbit trick: p - (((p + 1) & -(p + 1)) >> 1).

title: Maximum Side Length of a Square with Sum Less than or Equal to Threshold
summary: Find the maximum side-length of a square subgrid in an m x n matrix with a sum less than or equal to a given threshold, or return 0 if none exists.
approach: Precompute 2D prefix sums to evaluate any square sum in O(1). Greedily scan the matrix maintaining the maximum side length found so far, checking if a square of side maxLen + 1 ending at each cell satisfies the threshold constraint.

title: Largest Magic Square
summary: Find the maximum side length k of a magic square subgrid within an m x n integer grid where all row, column, and diagonal sums are equal.
approach: Precompute 1D prefix sums for rows and columns. Iterate side length k from min(m, n) down to 2, validating each k x k candidate in O(k) time using prefix sums and diagonal checks. Return the first valid k found, or 1 if none exist.

title: Find the Largest Area of Square Inside Two Rectangles
summary: Find the maximum area of a square that can fit inside the intersecting region of at least two rectangles.
approach: Iterate through all pairs of rectangles (i, j) to compute their overlapping width and height. For each intersecting pair, the maximum square side is min(width, height). Track the global maximum side and return maxSide^2.

title: Maximum Square Area by Removing Fences From a Field
summary: Find the maximum area of a square field formed by keeping two horizontal and two vertical fences and removing all fences in between, modulo 10^9 + 7.
approach: Include the boundary fences 1 and m (or n). Any pair of fences creates a valid side length. Store all pairwise horizontal fence differences in a hash set, then iterate through all vertical fence differences to find the maximum common side length.

title: Maximize Area of Square Hole in Grid
summary: Find the maximum area of a square-shaped hole formed in a grid of unit cells by removing a subset of allowed horizontal and vertical bars.
approach: Sort the removable horizontal and vertical bars to find the longest contiguous consecutive run in each dimension. The maximum continuous gap created is (longestConsecutive + 1). The maximum square hole side is min(maxHGap, maxVGap), yielding an area of side^2.
timeComplexity: O(H * log H + V * log V)

title: Separate Squares II
summary: Find the minimum y-coordinate of a horizontal line such that the total area of the union of squares above the line equals the total area of the union of squares below the line.
approach: Model square boundaries as horizontal sweep-line events along the y-axis and use coordinate compression with a Segment Tree over x-intervals to compute the union width of each horizontal strip. Calculate the total union area and find the exact splitting line via linear interpolation within the target strip.

title: Separate Squares I
summary: Find the minimum y-coordinate of a horizontal line such that the total area of squares above the line equals the total area of squares below the line.
approach: The area below any horizontal line is a monotonic function of y. Calculate half of the total square area and apply binary search over y in [0, max(y + l)] for 80 iterations to achieve optimal precision.

title: Minimum Time Visiting All Points
summary: Given a sequence of points on a 2D plane, calculate the minimum time in seconds required to visit all points in order when moving horizontally, vertically, or diagonally.
approach: The minimum time to travel between any two consecutive points is their Chebyshev distance, which equals max(|x2 - x1|, |y2 - y1|). Iterate through adjacent point pairs and accumulate these distances.

title: Maximal Rectangle
summary: Given a binary matrix filled with 0s and 1s, find the largest rectangle containing only 1s and return its area.
approach: Reduce each row to a Largest Rectangle in Histogram problem by maintaining running heights of contiguous 1s for each column. Process each histogram using a monotonic increasing stack in linear time.

title: Minimum ASCII Delete Sum for Two Strings
summary: Given two strings s1 and s2, return the lowest ASCII sum of deleted characters to make the two strings equal.
approach: Apply 2D dynamic programming where dp[i][j] represents the minimum ASCII deletion cost to equalize prefixes s1[0..i-1] and s2[0..j-1]. If s1[i-1] equals s2[j-1], transition directly from dp[i-1][j-1]; otherwise choose the minimum cost between deleting s1[i-1] or s2[j-1].

title: Smallest Subtree with all the Deepest Nodes
summary: Given the root of a binary tree, return the smallest subtree that contains all the deepest nodes.
approach: Use a single post-order DFS returning the maximum depth and the lowest common ancestor (LCA) node. If left and right child depths match, the current node is the LCA; otherwise, propagate the deeper subtree result.

title: Max Dot Product of Two Subsequences
summary: Return the maximum dot product between non-empty subsequences of nums1 and nums2 with the same length.
approach: Apply 2D dynamic programming similar to LCS. At each state (i, j), transition by taking both elements (optionally extending previous positive subsequence), skipping from nums1, or skipping from nums2.

title: Maximum Product of Splitted Binary Tree
summary: Split a binary tree into two subtrees by removing one edge such that the product of the sums of the two subtrees is maximized modulo 10^9 + 7.
approach: Compute all subtree sums via post-order DFS traversal. For each subtree sum S, the split yields products S * (totalSum - S). Find the maximal product using 64-bit integers before taking the modulo 10^9 + 7.

title: Maximum Level Sum of a Binary Tree
summary: Given the root of a binary tree, return the smallest level index x such that the sum of all node values at level x is maximal.
approach: Perform a Breadth-First Search (level-order traversal) using a queue. Sum node values level by level and update the answer level only upon discovering a strictly greater sum to naturally favor the smaller level on ties.

title: Maximum Matrix Sum
summary: Maximize the sum of an n x n matrix where adjacent pairs of elements can be multiplied by -1 any number of times.
approach: Flipping adjacent signs preserves the parity of negative counts and allows negative signs to travel across the grid. If the count of negative numbers is even, all values become positive; if odd, leave the negative sign on the cell with minimum absolute value.

title: Four Divisors
summary: Given an integer array nums, return the sum of divisors of the integers that have exactly four divisors.
approach: For each number, iterate divisors up to its square root. Pair each divisor with its quotient, pruning early if divisor count exceeds 4. Accumulate the sum for numbers with exactly 4 divisors.

title: Number of Ways to Paint N × 3 Grid
summary: Given an n x 3 grid, compute the number of valid colorings using Red, Yellow, and Green such that no two adjacent cells share the same color modulo 10^9 + 7.
approach: Classify single-row configurations into two symmetric classes: 2-color patterns (ABA, 6 ways) and 3-color patterns (ABC, 6 ways). Formulate transition counts between adjacent rows and apply dynamic programming with O(1) space.

title: N-Repeated Element in Size 2N Array
summary: Return the element that is repeated n times in an integer array of size 2n containing n + 1 unique elements.
approach: Traverse the array while tracking visited elements in a hash set. Because all other elements occur strictly once, the very first duplicate encountered is guaranteed to be the n-repeated answer.

title: Plus One
summary: Increment a large integer represented as an integer array of digits by one and return the resulting array.
approach: Traverse the digits from right to left. Increment the first digit strictly less than 9 and return immediately; otherwise set it to 0 and propagate the carry. If all digits were 9, allocate a new array of size n + 1 with leading 1.
